integrity.claim_type: analytic equality-case theorem for the first-order Banach Welch bound
integrity.computation_role: no computation is used as proof; verification is symbolic from trace identities and equality conditions

scientific_limitations: The theorem retains the diagonalizable nonnegative-spectrum hypothesis on the frame operator from the motivating Banach Welch bound.
The theorem does not address continuous or higher-order Welch bounds and does not prove existence of equality cases for arbitrary Banach spaces.

The motivating source has a notation/convention ambiguity between off-diagonal modulus and squared modulus; the claim is stated directly with the modulus M and translates the squared-modulus parameter explicitly.
A residual priority risk remains from unindexed later work that may have answered Question 3.12(i) under equivalent terminology.
title: Equality in the Banach Welch bound forces tight equiangularity
